abstract: LLM assistants increasingly ask clarifying questions (CQs) to elicit preferences and tailor recommendations. Although prior work emphasizes improvements in answer quality and user experience, how CQs shape users' subsequent engagement and reliance remains unclear. We conducted a controlled experiment (N=180) across six everyday decision scenarios, comparing human-LLM interaction with and without CQs. We further manipulated whether responses violated explicit constraints and whether violations occurred in the sub-decisions the CQs addressed, while preserving elicited preferences. CQs increased perceived understanding and satisfaction, yet participants spent less time reviewing and evaluating responses and accepted more responses unchanged, including erroneous ones. Within the CQ condition, participants more often accepted responses containing CQ-adjacent violations than nonadjacent violations. These findings demonstrate that LLM's proactive CQs shape subsequent engagement and reliance with preference elicitation. We discuss implications for designing and evaluating proactive assistants that support continued user scrutiny of answers alongside personalization.

ur.ai_reason: 受控实验检验澄清问题对用户依赖的影响
ur.tldr: 180人受控实验发现，LLM主动澄清问题能提升用户理解感与满意度，却缩短答案审查和评估时间，增加对错误回答的无条件接受，且对澄清所涉子决策的错误影响更明显。

title: Is That Clear? The Impacts of Clarifying Questions on Human-LLM Interaction
title_zh: 这清楚吗：澄清问题对人类与LLM交互的影响
